home-energy-audit.h1: Home energy audits in Sherwood Park
home-energy-audit.title: Home energy audits in Sherwood Park: EnerGuide evaluations, costs and rebates
home-energy-audit.description: Book an EnerGuide home energy audit in Sherwood Park: 23 licensed organizations, local prices, Alberta rebates and what 46% pre-1991 housing means for your upgrade list.
home-energy-audit.lede: 23 NRCan-licensed service organizations deliver EnerGuide home evaluations in Sherwood Park. Here's what one costs, what it tends to find in Sherwood Park houses, and which Alberta rebates it unlocks.

sections.h2: What an evaluation finds in Sherwood Park homes
sections.html:
Of Sherwood Park's 34,290 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 4% were built before 1961 and 46% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. The typical Sherwood Park house dates from 1991–1995, and an evaluation is how you find out what that means for yours: the blower door measures air leakage, the advisor inspects the attic, walls, basement, windows and heating system, and the report ranks upgrades by what they'd save.

Sherwood Park gets about 5,435 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −30.4°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Elk Island, the closest comparable location in that data set (29 km away). That's the 8th-highest heating demand of the 70 cities we cover. The more heating a climate needs, the more each fix is worth, which is why the evaluation's ranked list matters more in some cities than others.

In the Edmonton area, 79% of households heat mainly with a forced-air furnace and 8% with a boiler and radiators; natural gas is the main heating energy for 74% of households and electricity for 15% (Statistics Canada, 2023). The heating system on the report shapes the recommendations: a forced-air furnace invites a ducted heat pump, electric baseboards a ductless one.

sections.h2: What it costs in Sherwood Park
sections.html:
There's no provincial rebate or price list; the City of Edmonton's guidance is to expect more than $400 and to get two or three quotes.

Most providers quote the initial (pre-upgrade) and follow-up (post-upgrade) visits separately. Rebate programs that pay on measured improvement need both, so ask for the combined price.

• Initial evaluation, about 2–3 hours. The advisor measures and inspects the house and runs the blower door test.
  • Report and EnerGuide rating. You get the home's energy rating in gigajoules per year and a list of recommended upgrades with estimated savings.
  • Do the work. Most rebate programs only count upgrades done after the initial evaluation.
  • Follow-up evaluation. A second visit measures the improvement, which is what most rebates pay on.

sections.html: A blower door test is part of every EnerGuide evaluation rather than a separate purchase. There's no provincial rebate or price list; the City of Edmonton's guidance is to expect more than $400 and to get two or three quotes.

• A calibrated fan is fitted into an exterior door and pulls air out until the house is at 50 pascals, the standard test pressure.

heat-loss-calculation.h1: Heat loss calculations in Sherwood Park
heat-loss-calculation.title: Heat loss calculation in Sherwood Park: sizing a heat pump for −30.4°C
heat-loss-calculation.description: A CSA F280 room-by-room heat loss calculation for Sherwood Park homes, sized to the local −30.4°C design temperature: why it matters for heat pumps, what it costs and who does it.
heat-loss-calculation.lede: The heat loss calculation is how a heat pump or furnace gets sized for your house, and the key input is the design temperature: −30.4°C for Sherwood Park, from NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Elk Island, the closest comparable location in that data set (29 km away).

sections.h2: Why the design temperature matters in Sherwood Park
sections.html:
−30.4°C is the 7th-coldest design temperature of the 70 cities we cover. The F280 calculation works out how much heat each room loses on that design day, from the house's actual walls, windows, air leakage and ceiling insulation.

At −30.4°C, even cold-climate heat pumps lose capacity just when you need heat most. The room-by-room number tells you how much the heat pump can cover and how much backup heat to plan for, rather than guessing from square footage.

In the Edmonton area, 79% of households heat mainly with a forced-air furnace and 8% with a boiler and radiators; natural gas is the main heating energy for 74% of households and electricity for 15% (Statistics Canada, 2023).

Contractors who size by square footage routinely oversize. An oversized heat pump costs more to buy, cycles on and off, dehumidifies poorly in summer and wears faster. An undersized one leans on backup heat. The F280 report is the evidence either way, and it's worth having before you compare quotes.

About $150–$400 as a standalone calculation (a September 2026 planning range; quotes vary). Many energy advisors bundle it with an EnerGuide evaluation, which also gives the calculation measured air-leakage data instead of an assumption.

sections.h2: Why it matters in Sherwood Park

ventilation-assessment.title: Ventilation and humidity assessment in Sherwood Park: condensation, mold and HRVs
ventilation-assessment.description: Why Sherwood Park homes get window condensation and musty air, what a ventilation and humidity assessment measures, and when an HRV or ERV makes sense. 35% of local houses were built since 2001.
ventilation-assessment.lede: Condensation on windows, musty basements and stuffy bedrooms are ventilation and humidity problems, and they're easy to confuse with insulation problems. A ventilation assessment measures which one you have.

sections.h2: Why Sherwood Park homes get humidity problems
sections.html:
Sherwood Park gets about 5,435 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −30.4°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Elk Island, the closest comparable location in that data set (29 km away). On Sherwood Park's coldest days, window glass and poorly insulated corners get cold enough for condensation at humidity levels that feel normal indoors, so winter humidity needs to stay at the lower end of the comfortable range.

Of Sherwood Park's 34,290 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 4% were built before 1961 and 46% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Newer houses (35% of Sherwood Park's were built since 2001) are tight and usually have an HRV or ERV that needs balancing and cleaning. Older houses that get air-sealed can lose the accidental ventilation they used to rely on.

• Relative humidity in living areas and the basement.
  • Actual airflow from bath and kitchen fans, and whether they vent outside rather than into the attic.
  • How much fresh air the house gets, and whether an HRV or ERV is balanced.

faq.q: HRV or ERV?
faq.a: Both bring in fresh air and recover heat. An ERV also transfers some moisture, which helps keep very dry winter air from getting drier; an HRV suits houses that tend to run humid.

faq.q: Why did condensation appear after we got new windows?
faq.a: Tighter windows cut accidental air leakage, so humidity builds up. The fix is usually controlled ventilation, not leakier windows.

faq.a: Advisors assess ventilation and humidity during the evaluation; HRV or ERV sizing may be an extra service.

radon-testing.title: Radon testing in Sherwood Park: local levels, test kits and certified professionals
radon-testing.description: Radon in Sherwood Park: Health Canada survey results for the Capital Health region (1.4% above the guideline), how to test for 3+ months, where to get kits and C-NRPP professionals locally.
radon-testing.lede: Radon is invisible, has no smell, and is the second-leading cause of lung cancer in Canada. In Health Canada's national survey, 1.4% of homes tested in the Capital Health health region were above the guideline, and the only way to know about your house is to test it.

sections.html:
Health Canada's 2012 survey found 1.4% of 73 homes tested in the Capital Health health region above the guideline. The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 16.2% (1 in 6) of houses at or above the guideline for Edmonton Metro Area (Edmonton CMA).

The two surveys aren't directly comparable: the 2024 study pooled about 69,000 volunteer tests and more of them were taken in basements, which partly explains its higher numbers. Neither can tell you about a single house, because neighbouring homes can differ widely.

• Use a long-term test of at least three months, with most of it in the heating season, which gives the most conservative result.
  • Place the detector in the lowest level you spend four or more hours a day in, away from drafts, and follow the kit's instructions.
  • If the result is above 200 Bq/m³, Health Canada recommends fixing it within a year, sooner if it's much higher.

Our full radon testing guide.

sections.h2: Kits and professionals in Sherwood Park
sections.html:
• Alberta Lung supports free radon-monitor lending at libraries including Edmonton Public Library and Red Deer Public Library; long-term kits are sold separately.
  • For a professional measurement or mitigation, search the C-NRPP directory by your Sherwood Park postal code; it lists certified measurement and mitigation professionals.

• Alberta's building code requires a soil-gas barrier and a radon rough-in in new homes.
  • The Canadian Lung Association's Lungs Matter program offers up to $1,500 toward mitigation for households with low to moderate incomes or a lung cancer diagnosis.
  • If your level is high, mitigation (usually a sub-slab depressurization fan system installed by a C-NRPP-certified professional) typically costs $2,000–$4,000.

The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 16.2% (1 in 6) of houses at or above the guideline for Edmonton Metro Area (Edmonton CMA). Any home can have high radon, so Health Canada recommends testing every home.

faq.q: How long should a radon test take?
faq.a: At least three months, with most of it during the heating season. Short tests can't tell you your long-term average.

faq.q: Where can I get a radon test kit in Sherwood Park?
faq.a: Alberta Lung supports free radon-monitor lending at libraries including Edmonton Public Library and Red Deer Public Library; long-term kits are sold separately. Hardware stores and lung associations also sell long-term kits for about $30–$60.

faq.q: What does radon mitigation cost?
faq.a: Typically $2,000–$4,000 for a sub-slab depressurization system installed by a C-NRPP-certified professional.

mold-testing.lede: Mold sampling tells you whether there's a hidden mold problem and roughly where. It doesn't tell you why, and fixing the moisture source is the actual cure.

sections.h2: Why mold shows up in Sherwood Park homes
sections.html:
Sherwood Park gets about 5,435 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −30.4°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Elk Island, the closest comparable location in that data set (29 km away). On cold days, exterior corners, closets on outside walls and window frames get cold enough for condensation, which is where mold usually starts in Sherwood Park houses.

Of Sherwood Park's 34,290 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 4% were built before 1961 and 46% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Older basements without a moisture barrier and houses that were air-sealed without adding ventilation are common trouble spots.

• You smell mustiness but can't find the source.
  • After a leak or flood, to check that cleanup worked.
  • Before buying an older house with signs of past water damage.

If you can see mould, you usually don't need a test to know it's there; you need to fix the moisture and clean it up properly.

No Canadian province has a mandatory mould standard for homes. Health Canada's guideline sets no numerical limit: it says to fix moisture problems and clean up visible mould.

Ask any Sherwood Park tester which lab analyzes their samples, and look for one accredited under AIHA's EMLAP program for environmental microbiology. Pair sampling with a ventilation and humidity assessment, which finds the cause.

Ventilation and humidity assessments in Sherwood Park · Our mold and indoor air quality guide

faq.q: How much does mold testing cost in Sherwood Park?
faq.a: Plan on about $300–$600 for a typical sampling visit (a September 2026 planning range); lab fees for extra samples add to that.

faq.q: Do I need a test if I can see mould?
faq.a: Usually not. Visible mould needs cleanup and a fix for the moisture source. Testing helps most when you suspect mould you can't see.

faq.q: Is there a legal mould limit for homes in Canada?
faq.a: No. Health Canada sets no numerical limit; its guidance is to control moisture and clean up mould. Quebec has a voluntary handling standard.

sections.h2: Which Sherwood Park homes are at risk
sections.html:
Of Sherwood Park's 34,290 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 4% were built before 1961 and 46% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census.

  • Built before 1960: probably has lead-based paint (Health Canada).
  • Built 1960–1990: exterior paint may contain lead, and interior paint may contain smaller amounts.

Don't dry-sand, use a heat gun or power-wash it. Contain the work area, mist surfaces, clean with a HEPA vacuum, and keep children and pregnant people away until cleanup is done. No province has a lead-paint rule aimed at homeowners, but contractors in B.C. and Yukon must include lead in pre-renovation or demolition hazard inspections.

faq.q: Does my Sherwood Park house have lead paint?

faq.q: Are lead test swabs reliable?
